subject: gk
question: As a result of the green revolution, India was able to change its status from __________

options.text: a developing nation to a developed nation
an agricultural nation to a manufacturing nation
a slow growing nation to the fastest growing nation in the world
a food deficient country to a leading agricultural nation

solution:
The correct answer is __**a food deficient country to a leading agricultural nation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Green Revolution in India, primarily during the late 1960s and 1970s, was a period of significant agricultural transformation.
 
• It involved the introduction of high-yielding varieties (HYVs) of seeds, particularly wheat and rice.
 
• The revolution also promoted the use of modern agricultural techniques, including chemical fertilizers, pesticides, and irrigation.
 
• Before the Green Revolution, India faced chronic food shortages and relied heavily on food imports.
 
• The country was often dependent on aid from other nations to feed its growing population.
 
• The Green Revolution dramatically increased agricultural productivity, particularly in wheat and rice production.
 
• This led to a significant increase in food grain output, making India self-sufficient in food production.
 
• India transitioned from a food-deficient nation to a surplus-producing one.
 
• The revolution helped to avert potential famines and improve food security.
 
• It also led to a significant improvement in the livelihoods of many farmers.
 
• The Green Revolution had a profound impact on India's agricultural landscape.
 
• It contributed to the development of a more modern and efficient agricultural sector.
 
• The use of irrigation and fertilizers allowed for multiple crops each year.
 
• This allowed for a large increase in agricultural output.
 
• The availability of HYVs allowed for a much greater yield of crops.
 
• The green revolution allowed India to move away from being dependent on other nations for food.
 
• The green revolution was focused on increasing food production.
 
• It did not move India to a developed nation, nor a manufacturing nation.
 
• It helped stabilize the Indian economy, and helped to feed the population.
 
• The green revolution was a very important part of Indian history.
